title: Photo 140 · 머슬 아워글래스 BBW · 은입사 · 엎드린 자세 · 한국 50대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Korean woman in her late 50s, lines at the eyes, mouth and neck, warm ivory skin tone with a soft golden undertone, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, long micro braids falling to her hips, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears spiral drop earrings and has extra-long stiletto nails.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so long and vast that her head and her feet are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. Huge rounded shoulders and massive thick arms with the swell of the biceps and triceps showing through a soft layer of fat, a colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — a shadowed groove running around her middle, the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward, the muscle of her core firm beneath it. Below that waistline a great mass of soft heavy fat on her middle is squeezed out past her body on both sides where her weight presses it against the platform, spreading sideways into two or three heavy rounded folds with deep shadowed creases between them, the surface soft and uneven, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum. It merges seamlessly into her sides, her hips and her thighs with no boundary anywhere, one continuous body rather than a separate mass, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline, a gigantic powerful rear, colossal thighs with the great sweep of the quads visible under a soft layer, thick heavy calves with a diamond shape showing through, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body and her hands look small against her thighs. Wide at the bust, drawn in at the waistline, wide again below: the silhouette reads as a great hourglass at the most extreme size. Powerful and heavy at once, no bodybuilder leanness, the weight of the flesh visible in how it hangs over the muscle beneath. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is soft and loose at this age, every fold hanging low and settling deep over the one below it. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it spreads sideways and presses flat against the platform beneath her.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, coarse surface grain and fine crepey texture across the softest areas, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Korean eunipsa silver inlay style — a deep black ground with thick bright silver linework covering most of the surface, fine lattice fills between the lines, a bold silver band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs like contour lines. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Lying face down on the platform, her upper body propped up on both forearms with her elbows planted wide apart and her head raised and turned toward the camera, her legs straight and slightly apart, a colossal rear rising as two enormous rounded mounds far above the line of her back with a deep shadowed cleft between them, her broad heavy back built from massive horizontal rolls of soft flesh, her thighs flattening wide where they meet the platform, her body stretching across the full width of the frame from edge to edge.

Footwear: Extreme silver platform stiletto slides with a thick toe band, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the silver linework catching the light unevenly the way paint on skin does rather than like real metal, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation full-body photograph, wider than it is tall.
